title: Automating content analysis of scientific abstracts using ChatGPT: A methodological protocol and use case
author: Domínguez-Diaz, Goyanes, et al.

steps.title: Define codebook variables
steps.instruction: Create a codebook that lists each variable name, its description, the allowed values (if any), and any coding rules exactly as shown in Table 1.

substeps.instruction: Variable research_approach: description – indicates whether the research is Quantitative, Qualitative or Mixed; values – Quantitative, Qualitative, Mixed; rule – if the study has only one research method classify as Quantitative or Qualitative, if more than one method classify as Mixed.

Variable research_method: description – indicates the type of the main research method used to collect data; values – Methodological advances, Systematic literature review, Meta‑analysis, Big data, Experimental, Ethnography, Observational analysis, Case study, Discourse and textual analysis, Focus group, Interview, Survey, Content analysis, Network analysis; rule – order the values by descending priority when more than one method is detected.

steps.title: Construct prompt template
steps.instruction: Write a prompt that follows the structure of Table 2, inserting the role, task, variable blocks and the ending clause.

substeps.instruction: Role line: “You will have the role of a researcher that performs content analysis tasks.”

Task line: “I need you to code a series of variables based on {document_description}. Next, I will describe you the variables.” Replace {document_description} with the type of document (e.g., “abstract”).
For each variable add a block:
• “Variable “{variable_name}” which {variable_description}.”
• If the variable has defined values, add “Answer with one of the following values: {values}”.
• If the variable has rules, add “If rules {rules}”.

• If an explanation is required, add a line for a new variable named “{variable_name}_explanation” that returns an array of text fragments used to determine the value, limiting each fragment to up to 10 words.
Ending line: “All the variables are defined. This is the content to analyze (between triple quotes):”
Place the actual text to be coded inside three consecutive double‑quote marks ("""") after the ending line.

steps.title: Insert abstract to analyze
steps.instruction: Put the abstract (or other document) that you want coded inside the triple‑quoted block that follows the ending line of the prompt.

steps.title: Run prompt in chat mode
steps.instruction: In the ChatGPT web interface, send the prompt in two messages:

substeps.instruction: First message: set the role line as a system message.
Second message: include the task line, all variable blocks, the ending line and the triple‑quoted abstract as a user message. Separate each line with a line break as described.

steps.title: Run prompt via OpenAI API
steps.instruction: Programmatically call the model using the OpenAI Python client:

substeps.instruction: Import the client and call client.chat.completions.create with:
• model = "gpt-3.5-turbo"
• temperature = 0 (creativity not required)
• messages = [
{"role": "system", "content": "You will have the role of a researcher that performs content analysis tasks."},

{"role": "user", "content": "I need you to code a series of variables based on abstract. Next, I will describe you the variables. ... All the variables are defined. This is the content to analyze (between triple quotes):
"""
<your abstract here>
""""}
Request the response in JSON format and do not ask the model to repeat the original text.

steps.title: Collect and parse JSON response
steps.instruction: Capture the JSON object returned by the model; it will contain each variable’s assigned value and, if an explanation variable was requested, an array of up‑to‑10‑word text fragments for that variable.
